newsitem.title: KENYA: Moi's party rules alliance out of Kenya dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Moi's party rules alliance out of Kenya dialogue.

text.p: Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi's ruling party said on Tuesday an opposition-backed alliance demanding constitutional reforms could not join a dialogue on change.

After a meeting of the Kenya African National Union (KANU) party parliamentary group chaired by Moi, KANU said it had agreed on its team for dialogue on political reforms with church representatives and opposition members of parliament.
But it turned down a demand from the National Convention Executive Committee (NCEC), an opposition-backed alliance which has campaigned since May for reforms, to be part of the talks.

"It is KANU's view and position that any individual or group of individuals...which has disclaimed responsibility for the constitution and publicly adopted unconstitutional means for effecting change has no room in any democratic dialogue," it said.
The NCEC has called rallies since May to pressure Moi, 73, to agree to sweeping political reforms before elections this year and constitutional reforms after the polls.

The NCEC on Monday called for protest rallies on August 23 and blamed Moi's advisers for stoking violence around the Indian Ocean coast city of Mombasa since a raid on two police posts last Wednesday.
Moi blames the violence, in which at least 37 people have been killed in the region, on opposition leaders fanning tribal hatred before the presidential and parliamentary polls.
No date is set for the elections at which Moi, in power for 19 years, will seek a new five-year term.
KANU insisted on Tuesday that the elections had to be held this year, ruling out any delay as demanded by the NCEC.

"The constitutional obligation on the KANU government means ...the constitutional time frame cannot be held hostage to dialogue. The general election must therefore be held before December 1997," it said.
The KANU meeting condemned violence in Mombasa and called on law enforcement agencies to bring the guilty to justice.
Speaking at a news conference, KANU Secretary-General Joseph Komotho, who is also education minister, denied the government was orchestrating the violence to derail the reform process.

"KANU is for peace. It is for non-violence and will continue to stand on those principles," said Kamotho, adding that anyone breaking the law should be dealt with as an individual and not a member of a political party.
Several political activists are among those arrested in a hunt by police, the army and the navy for attackers.
Hassan Haji, coast province deputy commisioner, said on Tuesday Emmanuel Maitha, a Mombasa KANU official, was in custody and being questioned. A total of 189 people have been arrested so far.
Haji said Maitha would be charged if it was found he was involved in the well-organised violence, which has focused on attacks on police and Kenyans from outside the coast region.
Security sources said Maitha is linked to a Coast Protective Group which had sought to keep coast land for local people.
Haji also said police were hunting for Omar Masumbuko, the head of a pro-KANU youth lobby group, for questioning over why last week he had often arrived at clash sites before police.
He said two arrested activists with the opposition Safina party, which authorities have failed to register, were released and two more would be charged with holding an illegal meeting.
